capacity_gross_kwh.notes: InsideEVs: 'US FWD: 71.4 kWh, rated up to 150 kW'. EV Pulse also lists 71.4 kWh for the front-drive bZ4X.

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists 64.0 kWh usable for the 71.4 kWh bZ4X FWD (MY22-24, European listing); the US/Canada FWD uses the same 71.4 kWh pack (InsideEVs, EV Pulse), 2023-25 unchanged. Bjorn Nyland measured 57.7-60.8 kWh on a European 71.4 kWh car, so the true figure may be lower. Page 1564 returned HTTP 429 to the researcher, so the 64.0 comes from a search snippet; EV Database's AWD page 1565 (71.4 / 64.0, read by the fact-checker) agrees.
Estimated: EV Database's AWD page (MY22-24) lists the same 71.4 kWh nominal / 64.0 usable figures for the 71.4 kWh pack; supporting cite for the FWD value.

chemistry.notes: Autopian (chief engineer): 'The bZ4X used two different nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) battery packs depending on the motor configuration'. EV Database also lists NMC for the 71.4 pack.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists 355 V nominal for the 71.4 kWh pack, the 400 V class; Toyota's chief engineer says the bZ 'still runs on a 400-volt electrical architecture' (InsideEVs).

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: 2023-25 bZ4X (US and Canada). EV Database lists battery preconditioning as 'No' for the 2022-24 bZ4X; Toyota's 2026 pages present battery preconditioning as a feature standard on the 2026 bZ (Toyota USA 2026 release; InsideEVs calls it new). No page for the 2023-25 cars describes a battery preconditioning control, so none is recorded. Weakest for 2025: North America unconfirmed, and the 2025 European update added it. Counter-evidence for the owner: Subaru's 2025 Solterra kit mentions an 'uprated battery conditioning system' (twin car, 2024 update) and EV Pulse's 2024 AWD review mentions a battery-heating valve; neither describes a preconditioning control.

dc_max_kw.notes: InsideEVs: FWD 71.4 kWh 'rated up to 150 kW'. EV Pulse: the AWD rate was raised to 150 kW 'matching the front-drive model'. Same across 2023-2025.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Toyota USA's 2026 release says the new 11 kW on-board charger is 'up from 7-kW' on the prior model, i.e. the 2025 bZ (manufacturer-relayed figure for the prior model, applied to the unchanged 2023-25 hardware). Conflicting figures: 6.6 kW (InsideEVs/Out of Spec 2022 US Limited AWD test; InsideEVs 2023 Solterra article; EV Database 2022-24 bZ4X), 6.7 / 7 kW (EV Specifications, Solterra), 7.6 kW (EV Pulse, 2024 AWD Limited review). Toyota is the only manufacturer statement and says 7. Owner decision: use Toyota's figure.
